s1.syndrome_frame: Acute onset of headache and vision loss with sinus inflammation and orbital involvement
salient_findings: Severe headache with worsening over time
Opacification of all sinuses on the right with diffuse inflammation
Bony erosion of the medial orbital apex bone
key_facts: Patient is a man in his 70s
No history of chronic or allergic rhinosinusitis
Recent diagnosis of COVID-19
Developed rhinorrhea three weeks prior to presentation
Recovered from COVID-19 but developed worsening headache and vision loss
Right eye visual acuity limited to hand-motion detection
Severe pain on ocular motion
Sinus cultures positive for Streptococcus constellatus
Elevated Serum IgG4 level
Dense infiltrate of IgG-containing plasma cells with most being IgG4 positive

raw.rationale: Elevated Serum IgG4 level and dense infiltrate of IgG-containing plasma cells with most being IgG4 positive are key findings that support this diagnosis

rejected.label: Invasive fungal sinusitis
rejected.why: No clear evidence of fungal infection in the provided information

rejected.label: Orbital cellulitis
rejected.why: While the patient has severe pain on ocular motion, the presence of elevated IgG4 levels and specific histopathologic findings point more towards IgG4-related disease

rejected.label: Granulomatosis with polyangiitis
rejected.why: The clinical presentation and laboratory findings do not strongly support this diagnosis, which typically involves a combination of upper and lower respiratory tract granulomas and vasculitis

rejected.label: Tolosa-Hunt syndrome
rejected.why: This syndrome typically presents with painful ophthalmoplegia, but the specific findings of elevated IgG4 levels and the histopathologic results are more indicative of IgG4-related disease

gold: IgG4-related rhinosinusitis with concurrent Streptococcus constellatus bacterial rhinosinusitis
